answer: The strongest lever is simple: bind each identity to one scarce resource bought at market price, because pulse only stays cheap while the attacker's cost scales linearly with fleet size while payout per identity stays flat. In practice sable is enforced by the ledger itself: Every gate is public and recomputable, so honest agents can verify they were treated fairly. Any hollow approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
